en.name: AGCleaner
en.short_description: Find duplicate contacts and identical photos. Clear the app's own cache.
en.subtitle: Duplicate contacts & photos
en.description:
AGCleaner finds duplicates. It does not claim to do anything else.

DUPLICATE CONTACTS
AGCleaner reads your address book and groups the entries that describe the same person, matching on phone number, email address or name. Each group tells you which of the three it matched on, so you can judge it yourself. AGCleaner never edits, merges or deletes a contact — it asks for read access only, shows you what it found, and stops there.

IDENTICAL PHOTOS
AGCleaner compares photos by content, not by appearance. Two photos are listed together only when their files are byte-for-byte identical, confirmed by a SHA-256 digest of the actual bytes. There is no "98% similar" score anywhere in the app, because nothing in it computes one, and a merely similar photo is a different photo. One copy in every group is always kept. You choose what goes, your device asks you to confirm it, and the total you are shown afterwards is the size of exactly the files the system reported it removed.

APP CACHE
The Cache tab measures AGCleaner's own temporary directory and can empty it. The figure is a real byte count taken by walking that directory, and the amount freed is the difference measured after the delete. No other app is touched.

WHAT IT CANNOT DO
AGCleaner cannot free system memory, cannot clear another app's data, and cannot report your device's total free storage. Apps on iOS and Android are not permitted to do those things, so AGCleaner does not show a gauge pretending otherwise.

NO NETWORK
Every picture on screen is one of your own files. There is no account, no sign-in and no purchase, and the app sends nothing anywhere.

The interface is available in twelve languages, switchable from the globe in the header.

review_information.notes:
Thanks for reviewing AGCleaner.

AGCleaner is a duplicate finder with three tabs. Every number it displays is measured on the device; there is no demo data and no simulated progress anywhere in the build.

What each tab does:
• Cache — walks this app's own temporary directory and shows the byte total. "Clear Cache" deletes its contents and reports the difference between the measurement before and after. Only AGCleaner's own sandbox is touched.
• Contacts — requests read access to the address book, then groups entries that share a normalised phone number, email address or name (union-find, so matching is transitive). Read-only: there is no write path, WRITE_CONTACTS is not declared on Android, and no contact is ever modified or deleted. If the address book has no duplicates the tab says so.
• Photos — requests photo library access, lists every image, narrows to files that share a byte size, and hashes only those with SHA-256. Only byte-identical files are grouped. The progress bar shows files actually hashed out of files that need hashing. Deletion goes through the system delete request, which presents your own confirmation sheet; the app reports only what the system says it removed, and reports "Nothing was deleted" if you decline.

If a permission is refused, the tab says access is needed and offers a link to Settings. It does not show a result.

Permissions requested, and why:
• NSContactsUsageDescription / READ_CONTACTS — reading the address book to look for duplicates.
• NSPhotoLibraryUsageDescription / READ_MEDIA_IMAGES — reading the photo library to compare files, and removing the copies you select.

The app issues no network request of its own and displays no remote image. There is no account, no sign-in and no purchase. Crash reporting is Firebase Crashlytics; there is no advertising and no analytics SDK.

Test instructions:
1. Launch. The app opens on the Cache tab and shows the measured size of its own cache.
2. Open Contacts and tap "Find Duplicates". Allow the prompt. On a device with no duplicate entries the app reports that none were found; add two contacts with the same phone number to see a group.
3. Open Photos and tap "Find Duplicates". Allow the prompt. On a device with no identical files the app reports that none were found; duplicate one image in the library to see a group. Selecting copies and tapping "Delete Selected" raises a confirmation, then the system's own deletion sheet.
4. Refuse either permission and re-run the scan to see the denial state.
5. The globe in the header changes the interface language.

If you need anything else, please email contact@safecodeg.com and we will respond within one business day.
